reasoning:
Both submissions make the SAME single functional change at the same site: in the promotion arm of make-move, `ld a,(mkPiece)` becomes `ld a,(mkSide)` before the `or b` that merges the chosen promotion code into the piece byte. That is the right fix for the reported symptom. The promo code is held in B (Q=5, R=4, B=3, N=2), and the old code OR'd in the *whole moving pawn* (WP=1 / BP=9), whose bit 0 is set; 4|1 = 5 (rook becomes queen) and 2|1 = 3 (knight becomes bishop), while Q(5) and B(3) already have bit 0 set and so survive unchanged. That matches the report exactly — Q and B correct, R and N corrupted, both colours affected — and taking only the colour bit (0/8) preserves the black case (4|8 = 12 = BR, 2|8 = 10 = BN). It also explains the collateral evidence: the inflated `promotion d3` perft (62603 vs 62379, extra queen mobility at depth 3) and the "incr key/phase/pst BAD" line, since the incremental zobrist/PST updates compose the promoted piece the correct way and therefore disagreed with the board. The fall-through `mkNoProm: ld a,(mkPiece)` path is untouched by both, so ordinary moves are unaffected, and both push and capture promotions flow through this one site. So on the fix itself the two are equivalent; the difference is entirely in what is wrapped around it.

correctness_risk: Y is the cleaner risk profile — one instruction changed, nothing else added to the source. X's fix is identical, but it inserts six continuation comment lines that begin with a single leading space (not the file's 8-space code indent) and contain non-ASCII characters (an em dash) and backticks in an otherwise plain Z80 source. Every mainstream Z80 assembler will skip to end-of-line after `;`, so this is a small hygiene concern rather than a real defect, but it is a nonzero added lexical/build risk that Y does not take. Hence 4 vs 5; the one-point gap reflects only the comment block, not the repair.

minimality: Y is tightly scoped — the diff is two lines and only one of them is a semantic change (the second line re-emits `or b` unchanged purely to hang a comment on it, a trivial demerit). X changes one instruction and adds a six-line comment for it, a 7:1 commentary-to-fix ratio, and part of that text is bug-report narrative ("which is why they disagreed with the board and `checkKey` reported BAD") that belongs in a commit message and will read as stale once the self-test passes. The extra scope is comments only, so it is not dangerous, but it is not warranted at that length either: 3 vs 5.

clarity: here X is genuinely better. It states the concrete encodings (mkSide = 0/8, WP=1/BP=9, R(4)→Q(5), N(2)→B(3)) so a reviewer can verify the bit arithmetic without opening another file, and it explicitly claims that zobrist.inc `keyUpdate` and engine.inc `pstDelta` already use the colour-bit idiom — which is the argument for why a single-site fix is sufficient to clear the "incr key/phase/pst BAD" line rather than leaving three places inconsistent. Y never addresses that, so a reviewer of Y has to go check those files themselves. Y's comment is still good and names the exact trap ("mkPiece|promo would keep bit0: N->B, R->Q"), but its first clause ("the pawn's type must go") is clipped and splits awkwardly across two lines. 5 vs 4. Against X's advantage, its comment wall visually breaks the flow of a short routine and the cross-file assertion is unverified within the diff.

Merge: Y, by a narrow margin. Both close the defect identically, and the axes come out 5/5/4 for Y against 4/3/5 for X. I would merge Y and lift the two facts worth keeping from X's block — the piece-encoding arithmetic and the note that the zobrist/PST paths already use this idiom — into the commit message rather than the source.

Blinding note: the stylistic asymmetry (X's cross-file references and self-test narrative vs Y's terseness) did suggest a theory about differing authoring processes. I set that aside and scored only the emitted assembly and its comments; the correctness verdict rests solely on the bit arithmetic, which is the same in both.
